title: SubSearch: Robust Estimation and Outlier Detection for Stochastic
SubSearch: Robust Estimation and Outlier Detection for Stochastic Block Models via Subgraph Search
summary: SubSearch addresses robust estimation of Stochastic Block Model connectivity parameters when an adversary can arbitrarily modify edges incident to up to γn nodes, a setting where standard SBM fitters are biased. The method performs simulated annealing over fixed-size connected subgraphs, minimizing the spectral-norm cost ||A_S - Qhat(S)||, where Qhat(S) is obtained by spectral clustering and plug-in estimation on S, and returns the best subgraph for parameter estimation and outlier detection. On a single n=200, K=2, γ=0.3 synthetic SBM, it reaches sum-absolute estimation error 0.05 (oracle 0.02; pruning baseline 0.353) in about 14 CPU minutes, and on the jazz network it identifies outliers and yields final cost 14.94.

target.statement: SubSearch reaches a final sum-absolute estimation error of 0.05 on the single-run synthetic SBM graph with n=200, K=2, Γ11=Γ22=0.65, Γ12=0.35, and γ=0.3.

why: The authors released everything the match target needs: the full implementation lives in robust_estim_sbm.ipynb (the paper's Code + Experiments sections), the synthetic SBM graph is generated in-code from the published parameters, and the jazz/polbooks/polblogs CSVs are already in the repo. There are no weights and no external downloads. The only work is mechanical: extract the code cells out of the 17 MB notebook (it has no .py files) and execute just the single-run synthetic experiment cell for C1 rather than the whole notebook. Runtime is the real risk: the paper reports ~14 min for that run on a 2.7 GHz dual-core, and our budget is ~20 min total including install.
est_runtime: install ~3-5 min; extracting cells ~2 min; C1 S.A. run ~8-14 min (single-threaded Python loop over t_max=1000 Metropolis steps, each a K=2 spectral clustering + SVD on a 140-node submatrix, so it will not use the 22 cores); oracle and pruning baselines <5 s. Total ~15-20 min.
scale_down_plan: Only if the t_max=1000 chain overruns ~12 min: shorten the chain (t_max=400-500, or cooling rate 0.98) or drop t_tol to 10 to reach the low-temperature plateau sooner. Effect: the returned subgraph is slightly less converged, so sum-absolute error typically lands in 0.04-0.10 rather than exactly 0.05, and the '5 of 60 outliers' count (C7) may shift by a couple of nodes — would be reported as partially_reproduced. C2/C3/C4 baselines are seconds and can always be reproduced exactly.
blockers: notebook is 17.2 MB with embedded outputs; naive `jupyter nbconvert --execute` would run every experiment (multi-run synthetic, jazz, polbooks, polblogs) and blow the budget by hours — must select only the Code section + the C1 cell

requirements.txt pins numpy==1.26.0 / scikit-learn==1.3.2 / scipy==1.13.1 / pandas==2.1.4; these do have cp312 wheels, so Python 3.12.10 is workable, but scikit-network is unpinned and may need a recent release
reported runtime (14 min) is a large fraction of the ~20 min machine budget, so the clean re-run has little headroom

approach: Use the released repo exactly as a full_release: clone/install the pinned requirements, then extract only the notebook's Code-section cells into an importable module and the single-run synthetic experimental cell for C1. The wrapper sets the documented seeds, executes the authors' C1 cell/classes unchanged, and does not run the multi-run, jazz, polbooks, or polblogs experiments. It then computes the C1 sum-absolute estimation error from the final SubSearch subgraph using the authors' spectral-clustering and plug-in estimator, records C2-C4 cheap baselines, and writes results/metrics.json. A tiny --smoke mode proves the same data flow before the full 1000-step S.A. run.
steps: Clone https://github.com/leobianco/robust_estim_sbm/ if absent and install requirements with `python -m pip install -r requirements.txt`; if scikit-network resolution fails, install a current scikit-network release explicitly.

Run `python extract_authors_notebook.py --notebook robust_estim_sbm.ipynb`; it must write src/authors_code.py and src/c1_experiment_cell.py, extracting only Code-section cells plus the C1 experiment cell matching n=200, K=2, gamma=0.3, t_max=1000.

Import-test src/authors_code.py with `python -c 'import src.authors_code'`; inspect src/c1_experiment_cell.py to confirm the experiment cell instantiates the C1 config and calls the author run() method, and record the result variable names used by reproduce.py.
Run the smoke test `python reproduce.py --smoke` and verify results/metrics_smoke.json contains finite cost and finite estimation error with the tiny config.

Run `python reproduce.py --checks` or equivalent: generate the n=200 C1 graph with graph_seed=12345, assert 60 outlier flags/140 inliers, check symmetry/no self-loops, build a connected |S|=140 initial subgraph, run one spectral clustering/Qhat/cost evaluation, and compute C2-C4 baselines.
Run the full C1 experiment with `python reproduce.py`; reproduce.py seeds numpy/python with 12345, executes the extracted author C1 cell unchanged, and times the run.

After S.A., recover S_best from the author result object or namespace, run the author spectral clustering/plug-in estimator on S_best, and compute sum_{k,l in {1..K}} |Gamma_kl - Gamma_hat_kl| over all K^2 entries.
Compute C7 outlier count as the number of true corrupted nodes included in S_best; optionally compute C2 oracle and C3/C4 pruning diagnostics using author baseline code.
Compare C1 to 0.05 with a 10% relative tolerance (accept 0.045-0.055), write results/metrics.json with value, pass boolean, seeds, config, runtime, outlier count, and baseline diagnostics.

If the full run exceeds about 12-14 CPU minutes before t_max=1000, use the documented scale-down only as a last resort: t_max=600-700 or cooling 0.99 with early stopping already active; record the shorter configuration and mark C1 partial if the value drifts outside tolerance.
smoke_test: `python reproduce.py --smoke` generates a tiny n=40, K=2, gamma=0.3 SBM, corrupts m=12 nodes, picks a connected |S|=28 subgraph, runs 3 S.A. outer steps with L_t=5, computes the spectral cost and sum-absolute error, and writes results/metrics_smoke.json. Success means the extracted author functions, graph generation, corruption, clustering, cost, and metric writer all execute end-to-end in seconds.
intermediate_checks: Notebook extraction: confirm src/authors_code.py is non-empty, imports cleanly, and contains the author SBM generation, corruption, spectral clustering, Qhat/cost, SubSearch, pruning, and filtering definitions; confirm only the C1 experiment cell was extracted from the Experiments section.

Generated graph: n=200, K=2, exactly m=60 nodes marked outliers, 140 inliers, adjacency symmetric, diagonal zero, edge count in a plausible SBM range for Gamma diag 0.65/off-diagonal 0.35 after corruption.
Initial subgraph: |S|=140, connected, and contains a mix of inlier/outlier nodes; spectral clustering with K=2 returns two non-empty clusters; Qhat(S) is 140x140 and c(S) is finite.

Baseline sanity on the fixed graph seed: oracle sum-absolute error near 0.02, pruning sum-absolute error near 0.353, pruning cost near 22.15, and pruning keeps about 27/60 outliers; large deviations indicate a graph-seed/corruption mismatch.
Runtime pilot: time 5-10 S.A. steps and extrapolate; if projected C1 exceeds ~15 min on this CPU, reduce t_max only after recording the deviation, because the paper value assumes t_max=1000.
Parameter check: K^2=4 connectivity parameters are estimated; compute the error over all 4 entries, not only the upper triangle.
Final result check: S_best should contain roughly 5 of the 60 outliers; C1 error should be near 0.05 within 0.045-0.055.
budget_plan: About 20-24 min total: 0-5 min clone and pip install pinned requirements; 5-7 min notebook extraction and import checks; 7-8 min smoke test; 8-10 min C1 graph/baseline checks and runtime pilot; 10-23 min full C1 S.A. with t_max=1000 and L_t=60; 23-24 min final metric computation and JSON write. C2-C4 baselines cost seconds. If setup or S.A. overruns, preserve the 10% tolerance check and record actual runtime/value; only shorten t_max/cooling if the full run is projected beyond ~15 min and mark any deviation as partial.

"""Map the structure of the authors' notebook: headings and code cells only.

Usage:
    python inspect_notebook.py            # print heading tree + code cell summary
    python inspect_notebook.py --dump N   # print full source of cell index N
"""
import json
import sys

NB = "repo/robust_estim_sbm.ipynb"


def load():
    with open(NB, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        return json.load(fh)


def main():
    nb = load()
    cells = nb["cells"]
    print(f"nbformat {nb.get('nbformat')}.{nb.get('nbformat_minor')}  cells={len(cells)}")
    dump = None
    argv = sys.argv[1:]
    if argv and argv[0] == "--dump":
        dump = int(argv[1])
    for i, c in enumerate(cells):
        src = "".join(c.get("source", []))
        if dump is not None:
            if i == dump:
                print(f"===== cell {i} [{c['cell_type']}] =====")
                print(src)
                print(f"===== end cell {i} =====")
            continue
        if c["cell_type"] == "markdown":
            first = src.strip().splitlines()[0] if src.strip() else "<empty>"
            print(f"[{i:3d}] MD    {first[:110]}")
        else:
            n_out = len(c.get("outputs", []))
            # size of outputs to hint at which cells are heavy
            osz = sum(len(json.dumps(o)) for o in c.get("outputs", []))
            lines = src.count("\n") + 1 if src else 0
            first = src.strip().splitlines()[0] if src.strip() else "<empty>"
            print(f"[{i:3d}] CODE  lines={lines:4d} outs={n_out} outsz={osz:9d}  {first[:90]}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

args.content:
"""Extract the authors' code out of repo/robust_estim_sbm.ipynb without executing it.

Outputs
-------
src/authors_code.py          every code cell of the notebook's `## Code` section,
                             in original order, verbatim (only a tqdm import
                             fallback is added so the file runs headless).
src/experiment_cells/cell_<i>.py   the individual `## Experiments` cells that make
                             up the paper's single-run synthetic experiment (C1)
                             plus its pruning / filtering / oracle baseline cells.
src/experiment_cells/manifest.json role -> cell index mapping.

Nothing here rewrites or re-implements author logic; it only lifts it out of the
17 MB notebook (whose outputs are stripped) so it can be imported.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import sys

NB = os.path.join("repo", "robust_estim_sbm.ipynb")
OUT_DIR = "src"
CELL_DIR = os.path.join(OUT_DIR, "experiment_cells")

# The `## Code` section spans these cell indices (see inspect_notebook.py output);
# determined programmatically below so it survives notebook edits.
CODE_SECTION_HEADING = "## Code"
EXPERIMENTS_HEADING = "## Experiments"

# Cell 4 is `!pip install scikit-network` (Colab-only) -> skip.
SKIP_CELLS = {4}

# Cell 5 imports `from tqdm.notebook import tqdm`, which needs a running
# ipython kernel; we swap in a std-tqdm fallback. This is an environment shim,
# not a change to the authors' algorithms.
TQDM_SHIM = '''try:  # authors' import, with a headless fallback
    from tqdm.notebook import tqdm
except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - no ipywidgets/kernel
    from tqdm import tqdm
'''

# Cells of the single-run synthetic experiment (C1) and its baselines.
EXPERIMENT_CELLS = {
    49: "setup_graph_and_generator",
    52: "configure_sa_experiment",
    53: "run_sa",
    55: "read_sa_results",
    58: "configure_filtering",
    59: "run_filtering",
    62: "configure_pruning",
    63: "run_pruning",
    64: "read_pruning_error",
    65: "read_pruning_cost",
    66: "read_pruning_outlier_count",
}


def load_notebook(path=NB):
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        return json.load(fh)


def cell_source(cell):
    return "".join(cell.get("source", []))


def find_sections(cells):
    """Return (code_lo, experiments_lo) indices of the two top-level headings."""
    code_lo = exp_lo = None
    for i, c in enumerate(cells):
        if c["cell_type"] != "markdown":
            continue
        first = cell_source(c).strip().splitlines()[0].strip()
        if first == CODE_SECTION_HEADING and code_lo is None:
            code_lo = i
        elif first == EXPERIMENTS_HEADING and exp_lo is None and code_lo is not None:
            exp_lo = i
    if code_lo is None or exp_lo is None:
        raise SystemExit(f"could not find {CODE_SECTION_HEADING!r}/{EXPERIMENTS_HEADING!r}")
    return code_lo, exp_lo


def main():
    nb = load_notebook()
    cells = nb["cells"]

    # find the end of the Experiments section: next top-level heading after it
    code_lo, exp_lo = find_sections(cells)
    code_hi = exp_lo
    exp_hi = len(cells)
    for i in range(exp_lo + 1, len(cells)):
        c = cells[i]
        if c["cell_type"] == "markdown":
            first = cell_source(c).strip().splitlines()[0].strip()
            if first.startswith("# "):  # next top-level section
                exp_hi = i
                break

    os.makedirs(OUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(CELL_DIR, exist_ok=True)

    # ---- 1. authors_code.py: all Code-section cells, verbatim ----
    chunks = [
        '"""AUTO-GENERATED by extract_authors_notebook.py from\n'
        f"repo/robust_estim_sbm.ipynb cells [{code_lo + 1}..{code_hi - 1}] "
        '(the notebook\'s "## Code" section).\n\n'
        "Do not edit by hand: every class below is the authors' implementation,\n"
        "copied verbatim so that the reproduction uses their estimator, their\n"
        "cost function, their corruption model and their simulated annealing.\n"
        '"""\n',
    ]
    kept = 0
    for i in range(code_lo + 1, code_hi):
        if i in SKIP_CELLS:
            continue
        c = cells[i]
        if c["cell_type"] != "code":
            continue
        src = cell_source(c).rstrip("\n")
        if not src.strip():
            continue
        if "from tqdm.notebook import tqdm" in src:
            src = src.replace("from tqdm.notebook import tqdm", TQDM_SHIM.rstrip())
        chunks.append(f"\n\n# %% ---- notebook cell {i} ----\n{src}\n")
        kept += 1
    code_path = os.path.join(OUT_DIR, "authors_code.py")
    with open(code_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("".join(chunks))
    print(f"wrote {code_path}: {kept} code cells "
          f"({sum(len(c) for c in chunks)} chars)")

    # ---- 2. experiment cells ----
    manifest = {}
    for i, role in EXPERIMENT_CELLS.items():
        c = cells[i]
        if c["cell_type"] != "code":
            raise SystemExit(f"cell {i} ({role}) is not a code cell")
        src = cell_source(c).rstrip("\n")
        if re.search(r"\.show\(\)|savefig", src):
            pass  # harmless: these cells only print / read attributes
        path = os.path.join(CELL_DIR, f"cell_{i}_{role}.py")
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(src + "\n")
        manifest[role] = {"cell": i, "path": path}
        print(f"wrote {path}")

"""Profile the hot path of the authors' S.A. step on the C1 graph."""
import os
import time

for v in ("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", "MKL_NUM_THREADS"):
    os.environ.setdefault(v, "1")
os.environ["MPLBACKEND"] = "Agg"

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
import numpy as np

import src.authors_code as ac
from reproduce import build_c1_graph, SEED

np.random.seed(SEED)
ns, G_test, gen, _ = build_c1_graph(ac)

# where does time go?
sol, _ = gen.sample_random_connected_subgraph(G_test, 140)

t0 = time.time()
for _ in range(20):
    G_sol = G_test.subgraph(sol)
t_sub = (time.time() - t0) / 20

A = G_test.subgraph(sol).A
t0 = time.time()
for _ in range(20):
    ok = ac.is_connected(A)
t_conn = (time.time() - t0) / 20

t0 = time.time()
for _ in range(20):
    sc = ac.SpectralClustering(2, affinity="precomputed", n_init=1)
    sc.fit(A)
t_sc = (time.time() - t0) / 20

t0 = time.time()
for _ in range(20):
    st = ac.SimulatedAnnealing._calculate_state(
        ac.SimulatedAnnealing(gen, ac.SimulatedAnnealingConfig(
            subgraph_size=140, n_iters_outer=1000, n_iters_inner=60,
            tolerance=1e-4, n_iters_tolerance=25, initial_temperature=None,
            cooling_rate=0.99)),
        G_test, sol)
t_state = (time.time() - t0) / 20

t0 = time.time()
for _ in range(20):
    nb = ac.SimulatedAnnealing._generate_neighbor(
        ac.SimulatedAnnealing(gen, ac.SimulatedAnnealingConfig(
            subgraph_size=140, n_iters_outer=1000, n_iters_inner=60,
            tolerance=1e-4, n_iters_tolerance=25, initial_temperature=None,
            cooling_rate=0.99)), G_test, sol)
t_nb = (time.time() - t0) / 20

print(f"subgraph copy      : {t_sub * 1000:7.2f} ms")
print(f"is_connected       : {t_conn * 1000:7.2f} ms")
print(f"SpectralClustering : {t_sc * 1000:7.2f} ms")
print(f"_calculate_state   : {t_state * 1000:7.2f} ms")
print(f"_generate_neighbor : {t_nb * 1000:7.2f} ms")
print(f"numba installed    : ", end="")
try:
    import numba
    print(numba.__version__)
except Exception as e:
    print("NO ->", e)

# steady-state chain timing (2 chains of 60)
sa = ac.SimulatedAnnealing(gen, ac.SimulatedAnnealingConfig(
    subgraph_size=140, n_iters_outer=1000, n_iters_inner=60,
    tolerance=1e-4, n_iters_tolerance=25, initial_temperature=None,
    cooling_rate=0.99))
state = sa._calculate_state(G_test, sol)
for chain in range(3):
    t0 = time.time()
    sa._markov_chain(G_test, 60, state, 2.25, state)
    dt = time.time() - t0
    print(f"chain {chain}: {dt:6.2f} s -> {dt / 60 * 1000:6.1f} ms/eval "
          f"-> projected full run {dt / 60 * 1000 * 60000 / 1000 / 60:6.1f} min")

"""Isolate cost: spectral_embedding vs KMeans inside SpectralClustering.fit."""
import os
import time

for v in ("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", "MKL_NUM_THREADS"):
    os.environ[v] = "1"
os.environ["MPLBACKEND"] = "Agg"

import sys
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
import numpy as np

import src.authors_code as ac
from reproduce import build_c1_graph, SEED

np.random.seed(SEED)
ns, G_test, gen, _ = build_c1_graph(ac)
sol, _ = gen.sample_random_connected_subgraph(G_test, 140)
A = G_test.subgraph(sol).A

from sklearn.manifold._spectral_embedding import spectral_embedding
from scipy.sparse import csr_matrix
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans


def t(f, n=10):
    f()  # warm-up
    t0 = time.time()
    for _ in range(n):
        f()
    return (time.time() - t0) / n * 1000


emb = None

def do_embedding():
    global emb
    emb = spectral_embedding(csr_matrix(A), n_components=2,
                             eigen_solver="arpack", random_state=None,
                             eigen_tol="auto", norm_laplacian=True,
                             drop_first=False)

def do_kmeans():
    KMeans(2, n_init=1).fit(emb)

def do_full():
    sc = ac.SpectralClustering(2, affinity="precomputed", n_init=1)
    sc.fit(A)

print(f"spectral_embedding : {t(do_embedding):7.2f} ms  shape={emb.shape}")
print(f"KMeans on embedding: {t(do_kmeans):7.2f} ms")
print(f"SpectralClustering : {t(do_full):7.2f} ms")

# how many Lloyd iterations does KMeans actually run?
km = KMeans(2, n_init=1, max_iter=1).fit(emb)
km = KMeans(2, n_init=1).fit(emb)
print("kmeans n_iter_:", km.n_iter_)

# is the embedding sane?
print("emb finite:", np.isfinite(emb).all(), "std:", emb.std())

# threadpool scan cost, measured directly
from threadpoolctl import threadpool_info
t0 = time.time()
threadpool_info()
print(f"threadpool_info()  : {(time.time() - t0) * 1000:7.2f} ms")

"""Does Python's cyclic GC cause the per-eval slowdown during the S.A. chain?"""
import gc
import os
import sys
import time

for v in ("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", "MKL_NUM_THREADS"):
    os.environ[v] = "1"
os.environ["MPLBACKEND"] = "Agg"

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
import numpy as np

import src.authors_code as ac
from reproduce import build_c1_graph, SEED

np.random.seed(SEED)
ns, G_test, gen, _ = build_c1_graph(ac)
sol, _ = gen.sample_random_connected_subgraph(G_test, 140)

sa = ac.SimulatedAnnealing(gen, ac.SimulatedAnnealingConfig(
    subgraph_size=140, n_iters_outer=1000, n_iters_inner=60,
    tolerance=1e-4, n_iters_tolerance=25, initial_temperature=None,
    cooling_rate=0.99))
state = sa._calculate_state(G_test, sol)

GC_ON = sys.argv[1] == "on"
if not GC_ON:
    gc.disable()

for chain in range(5):
    c0 = gc.get_stats()[0]["collections"], gc.get_stats()[1]["collections"], \
        gc.get_stats()[2]["collections"]
    t0 = time.time()
    sa._markov_chain(G_test, 60, state, 2.25, state)
    dt = time.time() - t0
    st = gc.get_stats()
    c1 = st[0]["collections"], st[1]["collections"], st[2]["collections"]
    print(f"gc={'on ' if GC_ON else 'off'} chain {chain}: {dt:6.2f} s "
          f"({dt / 60 * 1000:6.1f} ms/eval) | gc collections {c0}->{c1} | "
          f"objects {len(gc.get_objects())}")

"""Probe: does OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 reproduce the authors' first S.A. state?

The authors ran on a 2-core i5, so sklearn's KMeans chunked its Lloyd
iterations over 2 OpenMP threads. With 1 thread the partial-sum order (and
hence the clustering) can differ. This probe computes the initial S.A. state
and T0 under a chosen thread count and prints them.
"""
import os
import sys

n_threads = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "1"
os.environ["OMP_NUM_THREADS"] = n_threads
os.environ["OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS"] = "1"
os.environ["MKL_NUM_THREADS"] = n_threads
os.environ["NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS"] = "1"
os.environ["MPLBACKEND"] = "Agg"

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
import numpy as np

import src.authors_code as ac
from reproduce import build_c1_graph, SEED

print("OMP threads:", n_threads)

np.random.seed(SEED)
ns, G_test, gen, sanity = build_c1_graph(ac)
sa = ac.SimulatedAnnealing(gen, ac.SimulatedAnnealingConfig(
    subgraph_size=140, n_iters_outer=1000, n_iters_inner=60,
    tolerance=1e-4, n_iters_tolerance=25,
    initial_temperature=None, cooling_rate=0.99))
init_sol, _ = gen.sample_random_connected_subgraph(G_test, 140)
state = sa._calculate_state(G_test, init_sol)
T0 = sa._calculate_initial_temperature(G_test, state, 60)
print("initial estimation error (triu):", state.estimation_error)
print("initial cost:", state.cost)
print("initial outlier count:", state.outlier_count)
print("T0:", T0)

target.statement: SubSearch reaches a final sum-absolute estimation error of 0.05 on the single-run synthetic SBM graph with n=200, K=2, Γ11=Γ22=0.65, Γ12=0.35, and γ=0.3.
target.metric: sum over k,l of |Γ_kl - Γhat_kl| (empirical estimation error)
target.dataset: Synthetic SBM graph, n=200, K=2, Γ11=Γ22=0.65, Γ12=0.35, 30% node corruption

tolerance.why: Rule 4: the paper reports no repeated-run std for C1; the target is a continuous sum-absolute estimation-error loss, not an accuracy/F1/AUC percentage on a large test set, so use a 10% relative band (±0.005 around 0.05).

audit_summary: The target experiment is the right one: a single n=200, K=2, γ=0.3 synthetic SBM run scored by sum-absolute Γ error, using the authors' extracted SubSearch code rather than a substitute method. The clean re-run produced C1=0.057 versus the paper's 0.05, about 14% high and outside the stated 10% relative tolerance; the oracle (0.021), pruning error (0.353), pruning cost (22.1471), and retained outliers (27/60) closely match the paper. The S.A. run used the full t_max=1000, L_t=60, seed 12345, and cooling 0.99, stopping after 610 chains by tolerance, so this is not a scale-down; no hard-coded paper constants were found. However, the reproduction script exited with code 1 because the filtering baseline failed on a missing Results attribute, so R15 is missing and metrics_json was not saved. The C1 discrepancy is best attributed to single-run randomness and the unstated graph-generation/initialization details, not to a method substitution.

requirement_check.evidence: Clean-run graph sanity reports n=200, K=2, symmetric adjacency, zero diagonal, 9970 edges, and community sizes [86,114]; generation uses the extracted authors' code in src/authors_code.py.
The run generated exactly 60 corrupted nodes (floor(0.3*200)) via the authors' corruption path; this is the intended m=γn outlier budget.
The estimated Γhat and reported sum-absolute errors are computed from empirical edge densities on the selected subgraph, using the authors' implementation.
The S.A. objective is the spectral-norm cost: log prints cost=10.6455 for the selected subgraph and cost=22.1471 for pruning.
Candidate subgraphs are clustered with the authors' spectral-clustering routine using known K, then Qhat(S) is formed from the inferred labels.
The run starts from a connected subgraph of the required size, using the authors' S.A. initialization; |S|=(1−γ)n=140 is implied by the setup.
The authors' proposal step swaps a node inside S with an adjacent outside node while preserving connectivity.
Acceptance uses min(1, exp(Δ/T_t)) in the extracted simulated-annealing implementation.
Log confirms t_max=1000 and L_t=60; the code/run uses S.A. seed 12345 and cooling rate 0.99 from the paper setup.
Markov chains of length 60 were used and the run stopped after 610 chains under the t_tol=25, ε=1e-4 stopping rule.
The authors' adaptive initial-temperature routine was extracted and used; command ledger shows inspection of _calculate_initial_temperature.
The final subgraph was translated into outlier identifications; log reports outliers=4 for the selected S.A. subgraph.
Pruning baseline output matches the paper: error=0.353, cost=22.1471, and 27/60 outliers retained.
